children: HAL shares gained nearly 2% in afternoon trade on Friday after the company handed over the final two LCA Tejas FOC twin-seat trainers and HTT-40 Basic Trainer Aircraft to the Indian Air Force, while Dhruv Next Generation helicopters were handed over to Pawan Hans in Bengaluru.
Shares of Hindustan Aeronautics were trading at Rs 4,867.90 on the NSE at 12:43 pm, up Rs 79.90, or 1.67%, from the previous close. The stock later traded at Rs 4,857.60, up 1.45%.

According to the Hindustan Times, HAL Chairman and Managing Director Ravi K said the company expects to start delivering the LCA Mk-1A to the IAF by the end of this year, with the remaining radar, weapons and software-integration issues being resolved. Kumar, in his first interview since taking charge on May 1, said the aircraft was undergoing final corrections.
Speaking to ANI, Kumar said extensive software modifications were currently underway during the testing stage.

"For deliveries to happen, the aircraft should be ready for that; we are still not there yet. We are working very hard for that. We will resolve issues soon and start delivering," Kumar said while addressing queries regarding pending Mk-1A deliveries.
"During check-in, there are lots of issues. I can't commit. Lots of software is involved in this. This software requires changes. That's why I'm not committing to a timeline," he said.

According to the Times of India, HAL has made 27 Tejas Mk-1A airframes out of the total 180 ordered. The aircraft is undergoing final corrections, with further testing required for AESA radar and missile integration.

After delivery of the complete batch of LCA Mk-1, HAL will now focus on the pending orders for 180 Tejas Mk1A jets - 83 aircraft ordered in February 2021, worth around Rs 48,000 crore, and 97 aircraft ordered in September 2025, worth Rs 62,370 crore, the Times of India reported.

The delivery of the final two twin-seat LCA FOC trainers completes HAL's original 40-aircraft Mk-1 order, placed by the IAF in two tranches in March 2006 and December 2010. The first batch of HTT-40 deliveries is part of the Rs 6,838-crore contract signed in March 2023 for 70 aircraft.

title: HAL wraps up original Tejas order; CMD Ravi K says Mk-1A issues to be resolved soon, stock up nearly 2%
